audit_findings.title: The valuation mixes pre-Hatch earnings with a post-Hatch capital structure
audit_findings.magnitude: filed: $100.0 million debt, $2.695 million H1 2026 interest expense, $14.1 million Hatch revenue and $7.9 million acquisition and integration costs
audit_findings.mechanism: The OE anchor excludes Hatch operations and acquisition financing costs, while the bridge and common-equity claim use the post-acquisition balance sheet without deducting debt.
audit_findings.evidence: The results of operations of the acquired business will be included in the Company’s consolidated results beginning from the date of acquisition.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter mismatch. The omitted interest and integration costs overstate value, while omitted Hatch earnings may understate it. The net effect is unresolved, but it is reasonably capable of changing the conclusion because base value is $21.47 per share versus a $21.66 market price.
audit_findings.action: Recalculate equity-level OE from post-acquisition filed results, including Hatch revenue, operating costs, retention expense and revolver interest, and rerun all scenarios on the same June 2026 perimeter.

audit_findings.title: The latest-year anchor may contain material cash-timing and one-off benefits
audit_findings.magnitude: filed: $23.7 million decrease in cash taxes, $26.9 million decrease in vendor payments and $15.0 million prior-year legal settlement; the tax-payment decrease alone equals 25.1% of the $94.3 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Temporary working-capital or cash-tax benefits can inflate the selected OE anchor and therefore every forecast year and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Net cash provided by operating activities during the year ended December 31, 2025 increased by $86.2 million compared to 2024, primarily due to a $67.8 million increase in cash collected from customers, a $26.9 million decrease in cash paid to vendors and others, a $23.7 million decrease in cash used to pay income taxes and the payment of $15.0 million to settle legal claims in the prior-year period, which did not recur in the current-year period.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates large cash-flow drivers but does not establish how much entered the submitted OE calculation. The prior-year settlement principally explains why 2024 was depressed, while the 2025 tax and vendor-payment movements could inflate 2025. Given the anchor's full use in the DCF and the narrow base-value gap to market price, the unresolved normalization could change the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Produce the 2024 and 2025 OE reconciliations by line item; isolate cash taxes, vendor-payable movements and legal settlements; normalize demonstrated timing items; then rerun the scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Hatch retention compensation is absent from the earnings anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: filed: $30.0 million over two to three years, equal to 31.8% of the $94.3 million anchor in aggregate; $7.9 million of H1 2026 acquisition and integration costs includes accrued compensation but the retention portion is not separately quantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Service-period compensation reduces post-acquisition OE and near-term cash flows but is absent from the FY2025 anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: In connection with the acquisition, we have also agreed to provide certain continuing Hatch employees with retention packages valued in the aggregate at approximately $30 million, to be paid over the next two to three years.
audit_findings.explanation: The obligation and its aggregate amount are demonstrated, although its precise annual allocation and the amount already accrued are unresolved. Its scale relative to the anchor and the valuation's narrow base-case margin make it reasonably capable of changing the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the retention vesting and payment schedule and the amount expensed, accrued and paid through June 2026; include the remaining service-period expense and cash payments in post-acquisition OE before rerunning.

audit_findings.title: Uncertain tax positions are an unbridged claim on cash
audit_findings.magnitude: filed: $55.9 million of uncertain-tax-position cash flows with timing not reasonably estimable at June 2026; equal to 59.3% of the $94.3 million anchor, 3.9% of $1,419 million base equity value and $0.85 per diluted share if fully incremental
audit_findings.mechanism: Any settlement not already captured in forecast OE is a cash claim that reduces the bridge cash available to common equity or future OE.
audit_findings.evidence: We are not able to reasonably estimate the timing of future cash flows related to $53.0 million of uncertain tax positions.
audit_findings.explanation: The potential claim is demonstrated, but its timing, settlement amount and overlap with recognized liabilities or historical tax expense are unresolved. A full incremental outflow would exceed the $0.19 per-share gap between base value and market price, so it is reasonably capable of changing the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $55.9 million disclosure to recognized tax liabilities, interest and penalties and amounts already reflected in OE; model expected settlements or deduct the remaining incremental debt-like claim, then rerun.

audit_findings.title: RepairPal purchase-price holdbacks may be omitted from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: filed: $7.3 million outstanding at June 30, 2026; computed: 0.5% of $1,419 million base equity value and $0.11 per diluted share if fully deducted
audit_findings.mechanism: An unpaid acquisition-consideration liability would reduce the equity bridge if it is not already represented through the cash balance or OE.
audit_findings.evidence: As a result, as of December 31, 2025, $ 5.3 million of the general holdback and $ 2.0 million of the tax holdback remained, both of which were classified as accounts payable and accrued liabilities on the consolidated balance sheets.
audit_findings.explanation: The liability remains filed and should be reconciled, but even a full incremental deduction would move base value only from $21.47 to approximately $21.36 per share and would not alter the $15.03 buy-below conclusion relative to the $21.66 price.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the June 2026 general and tax holdbacks remain payable and are not already captured through OE or another bridge adjustment; deduct any incremental amount in the next rerun.
